newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cheetah from Britain is "mad cow" victim in France.
newsitem.headline: Cheetah from Britain is "mad cow" victim in France.

text.p: A nine-year-old male cheetah which was brought to a French zoo from Britain was put down last month after it was found to be suffering from mad cow disease, France's Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday.
It was the fifth case of mad cow disease, known to scientists as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), recorded in the world in a cheetah since 1992.
The animal's half sister died of the same illness in 1993 at Whipsnade zoo in Britain where it had lived all its life.
The animal put down in France arrived from Whipsnade in 1993. It began to show signs of the disease in December and was put down on January 20, the ministry said.

Britain, which has had thousands of cases of BSE among its livestock, caused a Europe-wide scare last year by announcing that BSE-infected beef might cause the fatal brain disorder Creutzfeldt-Jacob Disease (CJD) in humans.
